outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Can the edited scene be visually inventoried to locate the paper and candidate receiving object and describe their visible boundaries and occlusions for a narrower insertion investigation?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence permits a grounded inventory of the paper and candidate receiving object, including concrete boundaries, visible identifying features, overlap, and visibility limitations. A pass establishes inspectable context only, not confirmed cup identity or insertion. Report separately whether paper identity and cup identity are established, disproved, or unresolved. Fail if adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object; identify the decisive evidence. Unknown if framing or visibility prevents even a grounded inventory. Unresolved cup identity must be recorded explicitly and never silently promoted to confirmed identity.
nodes.binding: Inspect source and edit directly. Use the source only to locate the requested objects and compare appearances, not to certify the reddish object's identity. Describe the paper outline and the reddish object's exposed contour and dark marking; investigate whether these support a cup, another object, or neither determination. Consider the combined visible structure without demanding a visible interior as an absolute identity requirement. Distinguish image-plane overlap from entry into a container. Do not infer hidden geometry or stuffing from the hand's grip.

nodes.question: Within the scene inventoried by s1, does direct inspection establish actual paper entry into a cup or an intermediate stuffing action, rather than projected overlap with the reddish object?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the paper and a cup are established by concrete visible features and the paper visibly enters or occupies its interior, or visible deformation and crossing of its opening establish an intermediate stuffing action. Describe the boundary crossing, containment, and whether progress is complete or intermediate; do not infer motion from a grip. Fail only if adequate evidence establishes no requested insertion progress: the paper is wholly external to an identified cup with no entry or stuffing action, contact is demonstrably rim-only, or a required object is positively shown absent. A candidate positively identified as a non-cup can support failure only when the relevant scene is sufficiently visible to exclude another receiving cup or hidden insertion. Unknown if identity, paper boundaries, opening, or occlusion prevents distinguishing entry from overlap. Lack of a visible opening alone is not evidence of no progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, including its explicitly unresolved identity fields, and inspect the edited image independently. Examine the exposed reddish contour, dark line, paper edges, and any observable receiving opening, depth, enclosing wall, or boundary crossing. Test cup and non-container interpretations against visible features rather than the instruction. Paper in front of a rounded form, color changes, and hand presence are not insertion evidence. Retain uncertainty if the paper could hide the decisive structure.

nodes.question: Given the visual inventory and direct opening-entry investigation, does the edited image establish completed stuffing of the paper into a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if concrete evidence identifies paper and a cup and shows the paper extending inside it with visible containment, compression, or insertion sufficient to establish stuffing. Fail if adequate visual evidence positively establishes the full target is not met, including incomplete insertion, wholly external paper, rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether failure coexists with actual insertion progress or with no progress, without treating completion failure as proof of either. Unknown if identity, containment, or the distinction between completed stuffing and an intermediate state remains unresolved. Some paper may remain outside a successfully stuffed cup.
nodes.binding: Use s1 and s4_opening_entry as ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly for completed stuffing. Do not treat s1's inventory pass as confirmed cup identity or s4's progress pass as completion. Cite the decisive containment or compression cues and reconcile any disagreement with ancestor observations using visible evidence. Do not infer an interior hidden behind the sheet, require preservation of the source cup's color, or count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Complete requires grounded paper-and-cup identity, actual insertion evidence from s4_opening_entry, and affirmative contained stuffing evidence from s2. Partial requires positively established insertion or intermediate stuffing progress from s4_opening_entry and positively established incompleteness from s2. Absent requires s4_opening_entry to establish no requested progress using trustworthy external-placement evidence or adequately visible absence of a required object. Failure of s2 alone never establishes absent. Unknown applies when required identity, progress, or completion evidence remains unresolved, or observations conflict without a grounded resolution. A pass on s1 supplies inventory context only; supporting agreement is dependent, not independent confirmation. Do not infer new visual facts.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s4_opening_entry: The traces repeatedly treat the reddish object as unresolved, but the supplied source image visibly establishes a blue cup with a large open mouth; the edited image appears to retain that cup, with the paper overlapping its rim/front. This is a visual-evidence miss, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: every query is valid and s1 passes, yet s1’s inventory contradicts the source. Refine the binding to compare source and edited images directly and use the source to identify the receiving object, while still judging requested progress from the edited image. Then inspect the cup’s visible rim and paper boundary for actual crossing/containment. Do not infer insertion from overlap alone; if the paper obscures the crossing, preserve unknown. Conversely, if the visible geometry establishes the paper remains outside with no insertion progress, allow fail rather than defaulting to unknown. The reference ‘no’ constrains the aggregate, not the atomic check, so do not force this node to fail solely to match it. Repeated high-confidence unknowns indicate a systematic evidence/calibration issue, not stronger evidence.
s1: The binding overconstrains identity by telling the node not to use the source to identify the receiving object. Compare source and edit directly: the source clearly shows a blue cup with a large open mouth, while the edited scene shows a reddish object, so explicitly assess whether the requested cup is still present or whether the edit substituted/removed it. Then judge progress only from edited-image geometry: trace the paper edge against the cup rim/opening and distinguish crossing or containment from mere overlap. The current repeated high-confidence “unresolved” inventory misses salient source evidence and does not resolve whether any requested change progressed; calibrate uncertainty to the actual visible evidence, not a blanket demand for a visible interior. Keep occluded geometry unknown, but allow a negative progress judgment when visible evidence establishes no insertion. Do not force the atomic node to match the aggregate “no.” The traces are valid and dependency-free, so this is a visual-evidence/binding issue, not transport or schema failure.

observations.evidence: The edited scene is clear enough to inventory. The paper is a blue-and-white printed sheet with a roughly rectangular outline, held by a hand; its lower and side edges are visible, while the hand covers part of its upper-left area. A reddish rounded object is partly exposed behind the paper on the right, with a curved outer contour and a dark line across it. The paper overlaps the object in the image plane, but the visible evidence does not establish that the object is a cup or that the paper enters it. Paper identity: established. Cup identity: unresolved; the exposed contour and marking are insufficient to distinguish a cup from another object.

The paper is visibly held in front of a reddish rounded object, but the exposed contour and dark line do not establish a cup opening or interior. The paper’s edge appears to overlap the object in the image plane; no boundary crossing or containment is visible. The paper obscures the decisive area, so insertion progress cannot be distinguished from projected overlap.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence to distinguish partial progress from no progress. Both focus on whether the paper is already stuffed inside the cup; s1 treats paper not inside as fail, and s2 only resolves whether the target is complete. The fulfillment readout therefore cannot reliably identify cases where the paper has progressed toward the cup but is not yet stuffed inside. Its absent/partial rules require that distinction, so the saved evidence does not support the requested extent.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The program adds unsupported visual assumptions to the saved binding: it directs checks to locate a blue cup in the source and a reddish object with a dark marking in the edit, although the only supplied instruction is “Stuffing the paper into the cup” and no images or such details are part of the program’s evidence. These specifics can bias identity and relation judgments. The remaining checks largely preserve the requested relation and distinguish progress from completion, but this unsupported scene-specific guidance prevents acceptance.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: On direct inspection of the source and edited images, does the reddish object in the edited image correspond to the blue cup visible in the source, and does its visible structure support identifying it as a cup?
findings.criteria: Compare distinctive visible features and assess the object's shape and any visible opening or interior. Record identity as established, disproved, or unresolved; do not treat color or overlap alone as proof.
findings.evidence: The source shows a blue cup with a broad circular opening and a white sheet. The edited image shows a reddish rounded object behind the paper, with a dark line across it; the saved observations call its identity unresolved.
findings.rationale: The observations repeatedly leave cup identity unresolved, but do not investigate the source-to-edit object correspondence. Resolving that relation could clarify whether the candidate is the requested receiving cup, without assuming that it is.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: Inspect the edited image's paper–object boundary closely: is any part of the paper visibly beyond a cup opening or enclosed by the cup, or is it only in front of the object's exterior?
findings.criteria: Look for a visible opening or rim, paper crossing that boundary, and occlusion or containment consistent with entry. Distinguish actual entry from image-plane overlap; if the paper hides the decisive boundary, retain uncertainty.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows the paper overlapping the reddish object's upper-left area; a dark line is visible across the exposed object, but the paper obscures the contact region. Saved observations report no established opening, boundary crossing, or containment.
findings.rationale: The existing entry check records uncertainty but does not describe a finer inspection of the obscured contact boundary. This targeted check could uncover evidence of progress or confirm that the available view remains inconclusive; overlap alone is not insertion.

transactions.reason: Across all five traces, s1 passes an inventory while leaving cup identity unresolved, and the nested entry check repeats that uncertainty, blocking completion assessment. Repair the existing nested candidate at the four-check cap by investigating source-to-edit object correspondence and then edited-image boundary geometry. Unlike the rejected scene-specific guidance, these bindings prescribe comparisons without asserting colors, object identities, or expected results. Preserve separate progress and completion coverage and genuine occlusion uncertainty. This proposal requires structural validation, label-blind semantic audit, and fresh repeated forward verification.

actions.question: What paper and receiving objects are visibly present in the source and edited images, and does direct feature comparison establish whether an edited receiving object is a cup?
actions.criteria: Pass if the images permit a grounded inventory and comparison, even if a particular identity remains unresolved. Separately report source paper and cup identification, edited paper and cup identification, and source-to-edit correspondence as established, disproved, or unresolved, with visible reasons. Inventory pass does not establish cup identity or insertion. Fail if adequate edited-image visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A source cup does not by itself establish an edited cup, and unresolved correspondence does not prove removal.
actions.binding: Inspect both images directly. First identify objects from visible structure in each image; then compare candidate counterparts using contour, proportions, opening or rim structure, enclosing walls, orientation, and other distinctive features that are actually visible. Allow source evidence to inform identity when supported by edited-image correspondence, but do not transfer source geometry into an occluded edit. Test retention, alteration, replacement, and unresolved correspondence without presupposing any of them. A color change alone neither establishes nor disproves cup identity. Describe edited paper boundaries, candidate receiving-object boundaries, overlap, and precisely which regions are obscured. Do not demand a visible interior as the sole identity test, infer insertion from a hand grip, or infer any object from the instruction alone.

actions.question: Within s1's compared object inventory, does the edited paper visibly enter a cup or undergo an intermediate stuffing action, or does visible geometry positively establish no such progress?
actions.criteria: Pass if grounded cup and paper identity plus visible edited-image geometry establishes entry, containment, or an intermediate stuffing action at the opening. Describe the specific crossing, enclosing occlusion, or insertion-related deformation and whether it establishes progress only or potentially completed stuffing. Fail if sufficient visible geometry establishes wholly external paper without entry or stuffing action, demonstrably rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. A non-cup candidate supports failure only if relevant visibility also excludes another receiving cup or hidden requested insertion. Unknown if identity or an obscured boundary prevents distinguishing entry from external overlap. Neither lack of a visible opening nor failure to find positive insertion evidence alone establishes no progress.
actions.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, including its separately reported identity and correspondence findings, then inspect both images independently to test those findings. Source geometry can help locate a corresponding edited rim or wall but cannot certify an edited spatial relation. Trace visible paper edges through the contact region and compare them with the candidate opening and exterior boundaries. State which boundaries continue visibly, terminate through occlusion, or remain hidden; examine whether an enclosing wall occludes the paper in a way that establishes interior placement. Consider external foreground overlap and actual entry as competing explanations. Resolve ancestor disagreements only with concrete visible features. Do not treat a dark marking as a rim without structural support, presume a cup because one was requested, or presume hidden insertion because the contact region is covered. Preserve unknown when decisive geometry is genuinely unavailable.
